This means that any `ModelConfig()` instantiated without explicitly setting `fp4_weights` will now have FP4 quantization enabled by default.

Now I need to make sure the test suite aligns with this new default. There is a test in `tests/test_fp4.py` called `test_model_without_fp4_has_no_fp4_linear`. Its purpose is to verify that when FP4 is disabled, the model does not contain any FP4 linear layers. Previously, the test relied on the fact that the default `ModelConfig` had `fp4_weights=False`, so the test simply instantiated a config without specifying `fp4_weights`. However, after flipping the default to `True`, this test will now unintentionally enable FP4, causing it to fail (the model will contain FP4 linear layers, contradicting the test's expectation).

I need to adjust this test so that it explicitly disables FP4 by passing `fp4_weights=False` when constructing the `ModelConfig`. That will restore the intended behavior of the test.

Additionally, because the default has changed, it would be useful to add a new test that confirms the new default is indeed `fp4_weights=True`. This will guard against regressions and make the intention clear to future developers. A simple assertion that `ModelConfig().fp4_weights is True` should suffice.

I already attempted a quick `sed` command to strip `fp4_weights=True` from the test file, but that only removed one occurrence and left other references untouched (the grep still showed a line with `fp4_weights=True`). Rather than continue fiddling with `sed`, it's cleaner to replace the entire test definition block with a new version that includes the explicit `fp4_weights=False` argument and also adds the new default-check test.
